subject: Recap: Pilot scope, milestones, and decision owners — Koopman Systems
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Koopman <evan@koopman-sys.com>, Sofia Reyes <s.reyes@koopman-sys.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Pilot scope, milestones, and decision owners — Koopman Systems

Hi Evan / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain we heard, the goals for a 6-week proof-of-concept (POC), and a proposed set of milestones and owners so we can align on next steps. Please confirm or flag corrections.

Top pain / goals
- High per-request latency from your current on-prem model hosting (esp. peak batch inference for customer-facing features).
- Cost unpredictability when usage spikes; need predictable unit economics for pricing experiments.
- Goal: 6-week POC to validate 1) <100ms median latency for chat flows at 50 rps, 2) 3x cost reduction per 1k tokens via batching + prefix caching, 3) path to production with private VPC deployment.

Proposed POC scope
- Dataset: anonymized logs + 10 canonical prompts (you provide)
- Model variants: two open models we discussed (7B quantized, 13B mixed-precision)
- Metrics: median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, output-quality pass rate on your prompt set

Milestones & timeline (proposed)
1) Agreement on scope & data delivery — target: Apr 25 — Owners: Evan (Koopman), Hannah (Redwood)
2) Infra & access setup (VPC peering / creds) — target: May 2 — Owners: Koopman infra, Redwood ops (Aditya)
3) Initial baseline runs & latency tuning — target: May 9 — Owners: Redwood Eng (Aditya), Koopman ML
4) Quality assessment & remediation — target: May 16 — Owners: Koopman ML, Redwood product
5) Final results review & decision checkpoint — target: May 23 — Owners: Evan, Sofia, Hannah, Marissa

Decision process / criteria
- Technical: meet latency & cost targets above on the shared eval set
- Business: willingness to move to Dedicated or Private deployment within quarter if cost/latency validated
- Procurement: target PO by June if decision positive; procurement timeline appears to be ~3 weeks per your note.

Immediate asks for you
1) Share the anonymized sample logs and canonical prompts by Apr 22.
2) Confirm the internal decision owners for procurement and security (names + emails).
3) Confirm SOC 2 evidence requirements (we'll attach SOC 2 report, expect: in-scope controls, data retention notes).

Attachments: koopman-priorities.xlsx (one-pager I sketched during the call).

If that all looks right I'll loop in Aditya (our tech lead) and Marissa (your account renewal/exec sponsor) to start the SOW and infra details.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for teams

Hannah — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Confirming a few items and one adjustment to timing.

- Scope: agree on the 6-week POC parameters you listed.
- Data delivery: we can deliver anonymized logs and 10 canonical prompts, target Apr 24 (one day later than your ask).
- Procurement owner: Sofia Reyes (s.reyes@koopman-sys.com) will own procurement. Security owner: Miguel Ortega (miguel.ortega@koopman-sys.com). Please add them to future threads.
- SOC2: we require the latest SOC 2 Type II for vendor validation; can you provide that artifact?
- Timeline tweak: our infra team is in hiring freeze next week, so can we push the infra & access setup to May 5 (instead of May 2)? Other milestones can move one business day accordingly.

Also, can you send a draft SOW and a short cost estimate for the POC (ballpark numbers are fine) so procurement can triage? If you can get a SOW over by Apr 20, procurement will start their intake and that should help hit a June PO target.

Appreciate it — Evan
Evan Koopman
VP Product, Koopman Systems
evan@koopman-sys.com

Thanks for the context — quick technical clarifications from my side:

- VPC peering: we support AWS VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. For the lowest-latency path we'll recommend PrivateLink; if Koopman infra prefers peering we can provide a checklist.
- Credentials: we need a read-only S3 bucket with anonymized logs and a short-lived service account for inference runs. We'll provide IaC snippets for the role.
- Model payloads: please confirm if you want token-level logging off by default (we can enable for debugging) — default is off for privacy.
- Schedule: I can be available for the infra kickoff on May 6 or May 7 (PST); either works for our eng calendar.

I'll take point on the infra checklist and upload to the Drive link Hannah mentioned by EOD Apr 21.

Aditya Rao
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
